title: Chapter 1: Understanding International Relations
content:
👋 ሰላም የEthioFresh ተማሪዎች! እንኳን ወደዚህ ልዩ የ Global Trends and International Relations (Chapter 1, Part 2: Sections 1.3 & 1.4) የቱቶሪያል ኖት በሰላም መጣችሁ! እኔ የ EthioFresh የፖለቲካ ሳይንስ እና አለም አቀፍ ግንኙነት አዘጋጃችሁ ነኝ። የዚህ ክፍል ዋና አላማ ዘመናዊው የአለም አቀፍ ስርዓት (Modern International System) እንዴት ከባለፉት ክፍለ ዘመናት ትግልና ጦርነት ተቀርጾ እንደመጣ፣ በስርዓቱ ውስጥ ያሉትን ዋነኛ ተዋናዮች (State vs Non-State Actors)፣ እና የአለም አቀፍ ፖለቲካ እንዴት ከሃገራት ወሰን ተሻግሮ 'Trans-national' እንደሆነ በስፋትና በጥልቀት የምንዳስስ ይሆናል። አብሮነታችሁ አይለየን👇👇

1.3. The Nature and Evolution of International Relations

The modern system of International Relations (IR) did not emerge in a vacuum; it evolved through complex historical struggles in medieval Europe. In medieval Europe, political power was deeply fragmented and localized among feudal lords, independent merchant cities, clerics, principalities, and duchies. Above these local entities existed two universal institutions asserting continent-wide authority: the (Catholic) Church (spiritual authority centered in Rome) and the Holy Roman Empire (a loosely structured federation of German-speaking and neighboring European territories).

👉 በ14ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን አውሮፓ ውስጥ ስልጣን የተበታተነ ነበር። በየቦታው የፊውዳል ጌቶች፣ የካቶሊክ ቤተክርስቲያን (ፖፕ) እና የቅዱስ ሮማን ኤምፓየር (Holy Roman Empire) ስልጣን ይፋለሙ ነበር።

From the 14th century onward, a central political entity—the State—began to emerge between the local feudal level and the universal imperial/papal level. Northern Italian city-states (e.g., Florence, Venice, Milan) played the Pope against the Emperor to gain independence. Kings in France and England began defying papal authority, notably exemplified by the French forcing the Pope to move to Avignon (1309–1377) and England's King Henry VIII repealing the Pope's right to levy taxes. The 16th-century Protestant Reformation (led by figures like Martin Luther and John Calvin) permanently broke the religious unity of Europe, allowing monarchs to establish state-run churches and appropriate church lands.

👉 የነገስታት እና የፖፕ ግጭት እየሰፋ ሲመጣ፣ ነገስታት የራሳቸውን ሰራዊት መገንባትና ግብር መሰብሰብ ጀመሩ። የፕሮቴስታንት ተሃድሶ (Reformation) የፖፕን ሃይማኖታዊ የበላይነት ሰበረው።

This political consolidation triggered internal resistance and massive peasant revolts across Europe (e.g., German Peasant Revolts of the 1520s, and uprisings in Sweden, England, Switzerland, and France). To defend their territories and suppress domestic rebellion, early modern states developed administrative systems, tax extraction mechanisms, standing armies, and judicial structures.

👉 ነገስታት ስልጣናቸውን ለማጠናከር ባደረጉት ጥረት በገበሬዎችና በህዝብ ዘንድ ከፍተኛ አመፅ ተነስቶ ነበር። አመፁን ለመቆጣጠርና ድንበራቸውን ለማስከበር አስተዳደራዊ መዋቅር፣ የግብር ስርዓት፣ ወታደርና የፍርድ ስርዓት ዘረጉ።

The Thirty Years' War (1618–1648) & The Peace of Westphalia (1648)

The culmination of these conflicts was the Thirty Years' War (1618–1648), one of the deadliest and most destructive wars in European history, reducing Germany's population by roughly one-third. While framed as a religious war between Catholic and Protestant states, it was fundamentally a geopolitical struggle for European hegemony (dominance)—primarily between France and Austria.

👉 በሃይማኖት ሽፋን የተነሳውና ለአውሮፓ የበላይነት የተደረገው የ30 አመቱ ጦርነት የአውሮፓን ህዝብ በተለይም የጀርመንን አንድ ሶስተኛ ህዝብ ያጠፋ አሰቃቂ ጦርነት ነበር።

The war concluded with the signing of the Treaty of Westphalia in 1648. This treaty established the foundational principles of modern international politics:

  • State Sovereignty: Every state possesses exclusive, supreme legal authority over its territory and domestic affairs, free from external interference (e.g., Pope or Holy Roman Emperor).
  • Formal Legal Equality: All states, regardless of size or power, are formally equal in international law.
  • International Anarchy: The absence of an overarching global government or central authority above sovereign states.
  • Diplomatic Practices: The institutionalization of permanent embassies, extraterritorial rights, legal immunity for ambassadors, and inviolable diplomatic dispatches.

👉 በ1648 የተፈረመው የዌስትፋሊያ ውል የዘመናዊ አለም አቀፍ ፖለቲካ መሰረት ጣለ። ዋና ዋና ነጥቦቹ፡ ሀገራት በገዛ ግዛታቸው ላይ ሙሉ ስልጣን አላቸው (Sovereignty)፣ በህግ ፊት ሁሉም እኩል ናቸው፣ ከአለም አቀፍ ሀገራት በላይ የሆነ ማዕከላዊ መንግስት የለም (Anarchy)፣ እና የኤምባሲዎችና ዲፕሎማቶች መብት ተከበረ (Diplomacy)።

Global Expansion and Colonization

Initially restricted to Europe, the Westphalian model spread globally through European imperialism, driven by the 19th-century Industrial Revolution's demand for raw materials and overseas markets. European powers engaged in the 'Scramble for Africa' and colonized vast regions, enforcing European concepts of nation-states, fortified borders, capitals, and foreign ministries upon non-European societies upon granting them independence post-WWII. Exceptions to European colonial rule included Ethiopia, China, Japan, Siam (Thailand), Persia (Iran), and Nepal.

👉 በ19ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን በኢንዱስትሪ አብዮት ምክንያት አውሮፓውያን ጥሬ እቃ ለማግኘት አለምን በቅኝ ግዛት ያዙ። በኃላ ላይ ቅኝ ግዛቶች ነፃ ሲወጡ የአውሮፓን የመንግስት መዋቅር (ወሰን፣ ባንዲራ፣ ወታደር፣ የውጭ ጉዳይ ሚኒስቴር) ኮፒ በማድረግ ዘመናዊው የአለም ስርዓት ተፈጠረ። ኢትዮጵያ፣ ቻይና፣ ጃፓን፣ ታይላንድ (ሲያም)፣ ኢራን (ፋርስ) እና ኔፓል በቅኝ ግዛት ያልተያዙ ልዩ ሀገራት ነበሩ።

😅 EthioFresh Humor Break: የ1648ቱ Peace of Westphalia የመጣው የ30 አመት ጦርነት ሰልችቷቸው ነው! ፍሬሽማን ሆናችሁ የአንድ ሴሚስተር የ

ኖት ሲበዛባችሁ እንዳይሰላቻችሁ፤ ቢያንስ እናንተ ከ30 አመት ጦርነት በኋላ ሳይሆን ከ4 ወር በኋላ ነው የምታልፉት! Courage!

1.4. Actors in International Relations

Traditionally, International Relations (IR) was strictly defined as political interactions between sovereign State Actors. However, in the contemporary era, the scope of IR has dramatically expanded to include diverse political entities, non-state organizations, and sub-national groups.

👉 በጥንታዊው አመለካከት የአለም አቀፍ ግንኙነት በሀገራት መካከል ብቻ የሚደረግ ነበር፤ አሁን ግን መንግስታዊ ያልሆኑ ተዋናዮችም ትልቅ ቦታ ይዘዋል።

1.4.1. State Actors

There are currently at least 195 sovereign states in the world. Despite their vast differences in size, economy, and military capability, all states share four foundational criteria:

  1. Defined Territory and Borders: Fixed geographical space demarcating where one state ends and another begins (except Antarctica, virtually all land on Earth is claimed by states).
  2. Sovereignty: Internal supreme authority over territory and external independence from foreign control.
  3. Government Infrastructure: Centralized apparatus including capitals, foreign ministries, armed forces, national flags, and national anthems.
  4. Recognition: Formal acknowledgment by the international community of states.

From a traditional Realist perspective, the international arena operates as a "world stage" where sovereign states act as the primary, rational, unitary actors navigating an anarchic system.

👉 በአለም ላይ ከ195 በላይ ሀገራት አሉ። ሀገር (State) ለመባል 4 ነገሮች ያስፈልጋሉ፡ የተወሰነ ወሰን/ግዛት (Territory)፣ የውስጥና የውጭ ነፃነት (Sovereignty)፣ መንግስት (Government) እና እውቅና (Recognition)። ሪሊስቶች (Realists) ሀገራትን የአለም ፖለቲካ ዋና ተዋናይ አድርገው ያያሉ።

1.4.2. Non-State Actors

The contemporary global system is heavily influenced by Non-State Actors that possess substantial agency and capacity to affect international outcomes alongside sovereign states. These include:

  • Multinational Corporations (MNCs): Commercial enterprises with headquarters in one state and operational facilities across multiple countries (e.g., Apple, Toyota, Shell). They drive global finance, production, and trade, often influencing currency exchange rates and national economic policies.
  • Intergovernmental Organizations (IGOs): Entities created by sovereign states through treaties to address collective issues (e.g., United Nations [UN], African Union [AU], European Union [EU]).
  • Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs): Non-profit, voluntary citizens' groups operating transnationally to advocate for human rights, environmental protection, or humanitarian relief (e.g., Amnesty International, Greenpeace, Red Cross).
  • Trans-governmental Networks & Individuals: Cross-border financial markets, international civil society, and influential individuals (e.g., political activists, media figures).

👉 አሁን ባለው አለም ሀገራት ብቻ አይደሉም አለምን የሚወውሩት! MNCs (እንደ Apple, Toyota ያሉ ትላልቅ ኩባንያዎች)፣ IGOs (እንደ UN, AU ያሉ በመንግስታት መካከል ያሉ ድርጅቶች) እና NGOs (እንደ Amnesty International ያሉ መንግስታዊ ያልሆኑ ድርጅቶች) ትልቅ ሚና ይጫወታሉ።

The Shift from 'Inter-national' to 'Trans-national' (Global Studies)

Scholars like Robert Keohane (2016) argue that the term 'International Relations' (which implies relations purely between states) is no longer adequate. Instead, terms like 'Global Studies' or 'World Politics' better capture current dynamics. Contemporary interactions—such as global finance, trade, labor migration, cyber threats, climate change, and terrorism—occur across state borders rather than through formal state diplomacy. Modern communication technologies, commercial aviation, and social media platforms allow ordinary citizens and non-state actors to project ideas, launch political movements, and initiate revolutionary uprisings rapidly without state mediation, effectively blurring traditional spatial and material boundaries of power.

👉 ታዋቂው ምሁር Robert Keohane (2016) እንደገለፀው፣ አሁን ያለው አለም በሀገራት መካከል ብቻ የሚደረግ (Inter-national) ሳይሆን የሀገርን ወሰን የተሻገረ (Trans-national / Global Studies) ነው። ሶሻል ሚዲያ፣ ኢንተርኔት እና የአየር ትራንስፖርት ሰዎች ያለ መንግስት ጣልቃ ገብነት ሀሳብና እንቅስቃሴ እንዲያሰራጩ አድርጓል።
